prompt: Use case: infographic-diagram. Act as a fresh independent image-model STYLE judge. Produce ONE clean, highly legible white scorecard, not new artwork. Images 1 and 2 are locked SAME-FAMILY building style crops. Image 3 is the locked original hut anchor and image 4 is the locked original shared-lighting scene. Image 5 alone is a whole-geometry candidate contact sheet of THREE exact existing game PNGs, columns left to right: hut, knapping_spot, woodworking_bench. Each column shows the same candidate at 2x nearest enlargement, actual 1x (64 px per tile), and 0.5x (32 px per tile). The enlargement is only for inspection; do not score labels, background, resampling pixels or the sheet as artwork. Judge the three candidates separately against the ACTUAL reference rendering language, not an idealized brief. Do not score the references, repaint assets, assume an expected outcome or use any historical scores. Use a table with exactly THREE rows and these columns: ID, MEDIUM, LINE, LIGHT, PALETTE, ONE-SENTENCE REASON. Give each candidate four independent integer scores 1 to 5: 1 unrelated, 2 substantially different, 3 mixed/noticeable drift, 4 close match, 5 indistinguishable rendering language. Four scores each at least 4 are required for model PASS; be strict and allow failures. Evaluate ink-and-wash technique, contour-to-detail balance, lighting direction, and natural earth palette. Judge depicted content and camera separately; different subjects or sparse materials alone are not style failures. Each one-sentence reason must identify the candidate content and an actual visual style difference or similarity. Add a final brief scale observation: the candidate hut wall is approximately 12–16 px at 1x, compared with the declared 16 px width of the new wall bands (6–8 px versus 8 px at 0.5x); state that the new walls are not pictured and this comparison uses declared scale, not direct visual verification. Keep every ID, number, full reason and scale sentence legible. Output only the textual scorecard, without decorative art, candidate redraws, or copied pictures.
